covered_actors: Providers of AI systems (including interactive, generative, agentic, and general-purpose AI systems, established in the EU or in third countries)
Deployers of AI systems acting in a professional capacity (including public authorities, agencies, EU institutions, and third-country deployers whose outputs are used in the EU)
Providers of general-purpose AI (GPAI) models (encouraged to implement model-level transparency measures)
Hosting service providers, online platforms (including VLOPs and VLOSEs), online search engines, broadcasters, and content distributors (encouraged to preserve markings and labels)
enforcement_authorities: Market surveillance authorities designated by the Member States
compliance_deadlines: 2026-08-02: Entry into application of Article 50 AI Act transparency obligations for all in-scope AI systems placed on the market or put into service in the Union (Article 113 AI Act).

2026-12-02: End of transitional period under the AI Omnibus amending the AI Act for providers of generative AI systems placed on the market or put into service before 2 August 2026 to bring systems into conformity with Article 50(2) marking and detection obligations.
penalties_summary: Providers and deployers infringing Article 50 AI Act transparency obligations may be fined up to EUR 15,000,000 or, for an undertaking, up to 3% of total worldwide annual turnover for the preceding financial year, whichever is higher (for SMEs including start-ups, whichever is lower). EU institutions, bodies, and agencies may be subject to administrative fines of up to EUR 750,000. Commitments under an adequate Code of Practice pursuant to Article 50(7) may be taken into account as a mitigating factor.
implementation_notes: Non-binding practical guidelines issued pursuant to Article 96(1)(d) AI Act; authoritative interpretation rests with the Court of Justice of the European Union (CJEU). Clarifies the four transparency obligations in Article 50(1)-(4) (interactive AI systems including AI agents, machine-readable marking and detection of synthetic audio/image/video/text, emotion recognition and biometric categorisation notices, and labelling of deep fakes and public-interest AI text) and horizontal clarity, timing, and accessibility duties in Article 50(5). Details exclusions for purely personal non-professional deployer use, sole scientific R&D, open-source components that are not AI systems, standard editing, law enforcement activities, and editorially controlled public-interest text. Compliance with Article 50 does not legalise practices prohibited under Article 5 AI Act or replace high-risk AI, DSA, GDPR, consumer protection, or accessibility rules. Adherence to an adequate Code of Practice under Article 50(7) facilitates compliance demonstration, whereas non-signatories must demonstrate compliance by alternative means and may face heightened supervisory scrutiny. No retroactive marking or labelling is required for outputs generated or manipulated (and, for public-interest text, published) before 2 August 2026.
